content.text: I'll price the example plan with a 5% price increase to show the impact on churn.

A 5% price increase raises monthly revenue from 51,000 to 53,500 cents (+2,500 cents) [E1]. Over 12 months with assumed 2% monthly churn, the churn-adjusted margin improves from 333,703 to 360,614 cents (+26,911 cents), because the higher per-month margin more than offsets the revenue lost to churn [E1]. The survival rate remains 78.48% regardless of price—churn itself doesn't change, but the economic value of retained customers increases [E1].
